sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Candidate faithfully preserves the required exact 150 kN/m standard alternative, the approved very-long-hatch reduced interval [100,150) kN/m, both applicability selectors, correct quantity units and decimal datatypes, and the actual-versus-required section modulus and shear area comparisons.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Make the unreduced design-line-load constant exact: add sh:maxInclusive 150.0 alongside sh:minInclusive 150.0 in gen:StandardLineLoadQuantityShape. The current minimum-only constraint incorrectly permits values above the regulatory 0.15 MN/m (150 kN/m) value. Preserve the approved very-long-hatch reduced interval of 100 kN/m inclusive to 150 kN/m exclusive and the actual-versus-required comparisons.

Preserve the exact 150 kN/m bound added per prior feedback, the approved reduced interval [100,150) kN/m, and the actual-versus-required comparisons. Repair the applicable alternatives so a very-long-hatch strip may still use the standard exact 150 kN/m design line load: the standard-load branch must not require veryLongHatchOpening=false. Permit either (1) exact 150 kN/m, regardless of hatch-length classification, or (2) only when veryLongHatchOpening=true and classification-society approval=true, a permitted reduced line load of at least 100 and less than 150 kN/m. Continue requiring abreastOfHatch=true and servesAsIceStringer=true for both compliance alternatives.

Candidate faithfully preserves the required exact 150 kN/m standard alternative, the approved very-long-hatch reduced interval [100,150) kN/m, both applicability selectors, correct quantity units and decimal datatypes, and the actual-versus-required section modulus and shear area comparisons.
